statement: A BST is given as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child; each placed node consumes the next two entries as its children. All stored values are distinct. A final line holds a new value x, absent from the tree. Insert x where the search for it falls off a leaf, then print the tree's inorder traversal. BST insertion creates no rebalancing here: walk down as in search, remember the last node, and hang the new leaf on the side the walk fell from. The inorder output must come back sorted with x in place.
constraints: Values and x are positive; -1 marks an absent child.
x is absent from the tree.

example.why: The search for 9 falls off 12's empty left side, so 9 hangs there; inorder stays sorted.

hint: In the recursive form, assign the child link to the recursion's return value - or the new node is lost.
mistake: Recursing into insert without reattaching the result; the tree prints unchanged.
